correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the grounded clique inverse, single-bridge rank-one split costs, and same-side diagonal inverse entries by unit-current injection and the cut-edge voltage drop. This exhausts all pair orbits; grounding both gateways is strictly worse than PP and omitting the occupied-side gateway in a colocated pair strictly increases cost. The exact SS−PG numerator over t(1+td_p) is q+(qd_p−α_p)t with α_p/d_p=(p+2)/4, which excludes SS even at p=4q−2. If p>4q−2, choose α_p>α_q and a sufficiently large finite bridge conductance: SS then beats PG and its limiting margin over PP, GP and TT is strictly positive. The example's PP–PG and PG–SS tie equations reduce respectively to 80−575t=0 and 3−15t/8=0; GP and TT cannot tie the optimum there. The stationary Brownian covariance follows from the positive definite grounded Lyapunov equation.
residual_risks: The result uses uniform positive internal conductances and a single bridge; no noisy leader or multibridge extension. The finite supplemental test logs are not the proof of the inequalities for arbitrary sizes and weights.

evidence: Lin et al. give the general objective and algorithms. Fitch–Leonard give joint-centrality formulas and exact path/cycle cases. Patterson et al. use resistance methods with solved cases in paths, cycles and trees.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These results permit evaluating a prescribed placement, but they do not classify the minimizing clique orbits for independently weighted clique interiors or give the existential size boundary.

evidence: The unit-weight record has only a split-to-split change. The present result compares α_p to α_q and needs separate finite-t dominance of SS over PG after their limits coincide.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Changing the interior weight ratio yields colocated and three-regime solutions not implied by the known split specialization; generic per-pair evaluation does not supply the sharp global parameter classification.

evidence: Leader-noise-free coherence is a grounded inverse trace up to the tracking variance factor of two. Effective resistance to the wired leader set expresses each grounded inverse diagonal.

value.rationale: The single-bridge network is a natural model of coupled communities. The formulas reduce all vertex pairs to five costs, and the strict four-to-one boundary is a parameter-independent obstruction differentiating bottleneck splitting from concentration. The ordered rational transitions show that supporting a same-clique optimum is not just a formal infinity-limit effect.
residual_risks: No complete phase diagram over all weight ratios is claimed.
